title: Royal Gardens after Oliver; Cliff King and Freddie Keppard at Harmon's Dreamland
summary: Wickliffe's band follows Joe Oliver into Royal Gardens around 1926. The next year Levy is with Cliff King at Harmon's Dreamland with Keppard, and King is a showman clarinetist.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: No, I think he was, uh, uh, I think he was playing, don't wait, am I wrong? Was, it was, did he ever play bass? He played bass, sure. Yeah, all right then, all right. I was wondering, I know he played trombone, he played with us too. We went to the, uh, Royal Gardens on 35th Street. You see, Joe Oliver had left, and he had went someplace. So with this band, we went in there, and, uh, can't think of it, we carried an awful good trumpet player, because we had, we had two trumpets. We had a, we had an awful good trumpet there to follow Joe Oliver. We had, we were there quite a while. And, um, I think that was about 1926, because I know the next year, I was with, uh, Clarinet King at Harmon Dreamland, and we had Freddie Keppard with us. I think Freddie Keppard was with Wycliffe then. Might use the, yeah. Yes, I'm sure Freddie Keppard was with Wycliffe. That was Cliff King, wasn't it? Cliff King, yeah. He played clarnet and saxophone at the same time. Yeah. And then he played the clarnet, and he learned how to bring it out of one side of his mouth. He got the air in one side and blew it out the other side, and he could hold a note, and we played Tiger Rag about, when we got to the trio, we played about four or five courses, and he held the one note, and he was kind of way up in the air. He was a great showman. He was a great showman, yeah.
He was a great showman, yeah. Sweatman and so forth. Yeah, yeah. A good pattern of showman, yeah.
But, uh, we had Freddie Keppard there with us, and he still was, he still was hot.
